title: Mixed-sign scarcity without legacy proportional scaling
purpose: Qualify the F-PM08D3 mixed-sign scarcity seam when a nearly empty Ribasim store simultaneously receives positive SWAP drainage and is asked to supply a larger negative SWAP infiltration transfer.
legacy_behavior_being_replaced: The legacy limiter can scale every secondary QDRAIN level with one net-shortage QDRATIO, including positive contributors. In external-owner mode this is not retained: positive SWAP drainage is incoming mass, while Ribasim-owned availability constrains withdrawals.
preregistered_relations: Direct cumulative Ribasim drainage equals each positive drainage input within 1e-6 m3; scarcity does not proportionally scale incoming drainage.
All realized infiltrations are nonnegative and remain at least 1e-6 m3 below the common 0.0051 m3 request.
Realized infiltration is strictly ordered C0 < C1 < C2, with C1-C0 > 1e-6 m3 and C2-C1 > 1e-5 m3.
Each final Basin storage remains nonnegative.
Each direct Basin mass residual closes within 1e-8 m3.
All cases are RECOMPOSITION_REQUIRED because the negative SWAP request is not fully realized; positive drainage is never clipped to manufacture feasibility.
interpretation_if_pass: The coupled external-owner profile replaces legacy mixed-sign proportional QDRATIO scaling with withdrawal-side Ribasim availability. Positive drainage remains authoritative incoming mass and increases feasible withdrawal, while negative-transfer shortfall is returned for joint recomposition.
nonclaims: No full real-SWAP recomposition loop is executed here.
No claim that the limited Ribasim infiltration can be committed on the SWAP side without re-evaluation.
